positiveControls: customer list and cancel are owner-scoped by Telegram user id
PostgreSQL trigger locks the active row and performs order insert plus trigger transition in one transaction
stored destination is revalidated before trigger
riskFindings: The watcher is a money writer because it creates a pending order without a separate immutable execution intent, client idempotency key or audit correlation record.
Price provenance is not fail-closed: get_cached_rate may return arbitrarily stale cached data or a hard-coded fallback after provider failure, and any positive value may trigger an order.

Confirmation has no replay/idempotency guard and does not repeat blocked-user or offering-policy checks, so duplicate callbacks, mid-flow revocation or a closed currency can still create active orders.
The database commit precedes Telegram delivery and the customer-send exception is swallowed, so notification failure can leave a silent pending order.
The deployed active scan and expiry update are unbounded; the bounded proposal is rehearsal-only and not deployed.
Customer success copy points to /limits, but that command is admin-only; the customer list is available only through the lo_list callback.
The label automatic purchase overstates behavior: the watcher creates a payment-required pending order; it does not debit the customer automatically.
The schema has no order_id foreign key, uniqueness or status-to-triggered evidence constraint, and customer history omits expired and cancelled rows.
blockers: no fresh authenticated rate-evidence fail-closed gate
